title: Learning: The Breach
text: The shop's database is stolen: every account's public key. Days later, a sign-in arrives from a device-bound key whose counter looks odd.
held: The stolen table signed nothing, and the counter moved the way it should.

cards.label: Carry on: a public key can't sign anything
Assume your account is open to whoever has the table
cards.why: A public key only checks signatures; it can't make them. That is the difference from a stolen password table.

cards.label: Stop and flag the account
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: signature counter
fields.check: Compare the counter with the last one seen
fields.ok: Higher than last time, as expected.

intrusion.why: Two devices are answering with the same key, and one of them is a copy. The counter is how that shows.
intrusion.reveal: The signature counter had gone backwards: a copy of the key was in use.

temptations.label: Accept it and store the lower number: they probably restored a backup
temptations.why: A device-bound key can't be restored from a backup; that is what device-bound means. A lower counter is a second device.

teaches: A stolen list of public keys lets nobody sign in.
For device-bound keys, a counter that goes backwards means a clone.
